title: Classical Oracle Separating QMA From the QCMA Hierarchy via Polynomial Switching Lemma
whyItMatters: Constructed a classical oracle separating QMA from the entire QCMA hierarchy—resolving a question posed by Aaronson, Ingram & Kretschmer—via a variable-independent bounded-polynomial switching lemma developed with GPT-6 Astra.
summary: Yiming Wang (arXiv:2611.23693, Nov 2026) constructed a classical oracle relative to which QMA (quantum proofs) is not contained in the entire QCMA hierarchy (alternating classical proofs with quantum verifiers), resolving a central open question of Aaronson, Ingram, and Kretschmer alongside finer collapses (QCMA = P ≠ QMA and QMA = P ≠ PP). The author’s explicit AI usage disclosure documents that GPT-6 Astra produced an initial proof of a weaker separation, contributed core proof techniques for the variable-independent bounded-polynomial switching lemma, and audited the final proof.
technicalHighlights: Proved a variable-independent switching lemma for bounded polynomials, conceptually unifying sampler-based arguments separating quantum from classical witnesses.
Constructed a classical oracle separating QMA from the full QCMA hierarchy (QCMAH), plus finely controlled collapse oracles for QCMA and QMA.
Explicitly credited GPT-6 Astra with producing the initial weaker separation, proof-technique exploration, and final mathematical audit.
caveats: Posted as a November 2026 arXiv preprint awaiting formal peer review (appearing concurrently with independent work by Cakan using different techniques), and applies relative to a classical oracle rather than unrelativized complexity classes.

scoreRationale.foundational: Introduces a variable-independent polynomial switching lemma resolving the classical-oracle separation of QMA from the QCMA hierarchy.
scoreRationale.ripple: Provides a clean conceptual tool for quantum witness complexity, switching lemmas, and connections to Aaronson–Ambainis.
scoreRationale.verification: Author-verified arXiv preprint with detailed proofs and concurrent confirmation of the separation, pending peer review.
scoreRationale.velocity: GPT-6 Astra accelerated the initial separation proof and full argument audit in days.
